commits.message: Merge the event-unknown bound and verifier-wait fixes into the PR 471 branch

Wait as long as the verifier's own bound for each validation worker readiness job

The readiness test's job timeout was 2 s, which a worker that loads its
module under a loaded host can pass before its verifier is ready. The
job now waits LEDGER_ED25519_READY_TIMEOUT_MS, the verifier's own bound.
The job's timer starts when the worker spawns and the verifier's only
once the worker has loaded, so a job whose initialisation never settles
still times out first. The node-exit, start and per-row timeouts scale
with it.

Name the outputs a retention-unseen refusal is missing

The follower refuses an external deposit or withdrawal as
retention_output_unseen only when an output its admission references is
absent from the facts. One the facts hold at another address, without an
inline datum or with another payload is refused as malformed. The
refusal's detail is the list of absent referenced outputs (txHash#index),
read back as typed outrefs, and the node's origin_after_frontier detail
names them. The operator text says to reset the follower store to an
l1Origin before the block that created each named output, found with
find-origin --tx, and no longer claims that a store at the documented
origin holds every retention output. The landed_block_event_unknown text
now lists an unreadable follower cursor and a block start that maps to no
slot.

Exempt the validation-case refusal redeemers by name, not by callback

The two refusal tests pass fixed indices on purpose: no case or thread exists
at any position. The merge wrapped them in callbacks that ignore the builder
context, which the redeemer-index rule trusts. They go back to plain
redeemers with a disable comment that gives the reason.

Initialize the DA bond pool and event history only from reference scripts

Fault-proof and protocol scripts always deploy as reference scripts.
appendDaBondPoolInitialization and buildInitDaBondPoolTxProgram now require
the pool minting reference, appendEventHistoryInitialization requires the
deposit and withdrawal list references, and the inline-attach branches are
deleted. The check that each reference carries the right script stays and
gains a refusal test. The SDK pool tests read the pool from a published
reference, and the real InitPool test measures only the by-reference size.

Tighten review loose ends in dispatch, tests and the source-read rule

- dispatch: a successful one-line reply counts as a login failure only when
  it opens with one, so a verdict that quotes such a message is kept.
- The scheduler-refresh negative now requires MISSING_SCRIPT, since local
  evaluation would otherwise let any failure pass it.
- The SDK timing test is named for what it checks, and the certificate
  index comment names what the builder passes.
- tests-observe-behavior lists its blind spots in its header, where
  docs/agents/lint-rules.md points.

Install the Nix apps with resolvable peers and check them as Docker does

- The app reinstall selects the production closure with --filter-prod but
  keeps each selected package's dev dependencies: workspace packages satisfy
  their lucid and effect peers through them, so the --prod install left
  midgard-sdk's imports unresolved and the node and DA apps failed to start.
- Like the images, each app output carries its native binaries and their
  .sha256 under native/, and the wrappers set only the environment the
  Dockerfiles set (NODE_ENV, and MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_ for the watcher)
  instead of path defaults that outranked an operator's .env.
- Nix CI starts every entry point after building, runs on any change to how
  packages build and on every push to main under demo, and keys its cache on
  the flake files too.
- Each file the toolchain check reads must pin its own tools, so a pin that
  turns into a form the readers miss fails instead of passing. The check now
  also covers .env.example, go.mod and the full-stack prerequisites, which
  replaces the go-pins source-scan test.

Build the toolchain and every Midgard process with Nix or Docker

Nix and Docker are now two independent ways to get everything that builds
and runs Midgard; Nix builds no images. Both take their versions from
demo/toolchain.json (pnpm from packageManager, aiken from flake.lock).

- flake.nix reads the manifest and asserts each package's version. The
  devShell carries Node, pnpm, Go, Rust, Aiken, PostgreSQL, cardano-node,
  Ogmios, Kupo and mithril-client; packages build the Go transport, the
  Rust MPF owner and the node, watcher and DA committee apps natively.
- Rust in the devShell moves from 1.94.1 to the Dockerfiles' 1.91.0.
- scripts/release/toolchain.mjs holds the Dockerfile, compose and CI pins
  to the manifest, run as the toolchain-pins preflight check.
- Nix CI builds every package when a lockfile, the manifest or a flake
  file changes.

Initialize the protocol only from published reference scripts

Fault-proof and protocol scripts always deploy as reference scripts, and
every caller of the atomic init already passes them. Make the reference
scripts (the DA bond pool and case configuration mints included) required
by the SDK and node init builders and delete the inline-attach branch
that no deployment reached.

Merge origin/colll78/canonical-v1-watcher-l1-source-checkpoint into colll78/af-p3-p6

Resolves the agent-friendly P3-P6 batch against the updated checkpoint
branch. The transition-trace field step now plans its step redeemer
against the builder's reference inputs, the adversarial validation-case
mints build their redeemers in builder callbacks, and the generated
deployment profiles ceiling covers the Aiken env constants it now
exports.

Exit on a late-origin store when the follower refused a named order for an unseen retention output

The follower now records the refusal of an external-payload deposit or
withdrawal whose retention output is not among its facts under its own
reason, retention_output_unseen, instead of malformed, and exposes the
refusals at or before a slot.

Foreign-block replay reads those refusals with the coverage. A deposit or
withdrawal a block names that the follower refused for this reason is a
store whose origin is too late for the block (origin_after_frontier). An
absent deposit or withdrawal is judged invalid only while the refusals in
the block's range are still in the facts, with the prune at or before the
range's start; past it, or with the refusals unreadable, the block waits
as event_unknown. The operator text for both reasons is updated.

Run the stress-wallet verifier rows through the CLI dispatch and list the event-unknown causes that remain

The stress-wallet consolidation and terminal-drain rows now run each
command through the CLI's own dispatch, so the dispatcher's failure path
is what exits 1. The landed_block_event_unknown operator text no longer
lists a late origin or a seeded node output, which end at
landed_block_origin_after_frontier; it keeps the late origin whose
protocol-init fact is unreadable.
Merge the second CI-reds batch into the PR 471 branch
Name the replay function, not a line, in the init-cover horizon comment

Bound the Ed25519 verifier wait in the committee, watcher, wallet and CLIs

The DA committee's startup now fails at once, as
committee_startup_verifier_unavailable, when the ledger's Ed25519 verifier
did not become ready within its bound. The process exits non-zero and its
supervisor's restart is the retry, since the outcome is settled for the
life of the process. The committee handlers and the reconciler, the
watcher's startup, the lucid-midgard builder, witness import and wallet
signing, and the fault-proofs and stress-wallets CLIs each surface the
typed error, or exit non-zero with its message. The fault-proofs CLI body
moves into bin.run-cli.ts so that it can be run in a test.
